title: Group: legal entity register and organization charts
source_system: Corporate secretary's entity management system; treasury and operations confirmations
what_it_shows: A holding company (SEC registrant) with three separate subsidiaries under common ownership: Staffing (NAICS 561320), Professional Services and Consulting (NAICS 541512) and Home Health (NAICS 621610, acquired 2023). Corporate shared services (identity, network, security operations, cloud, the Group Workforce Platform, finance, legal) sit in the parent. Each subsidiary and corporate is a separate employing entity. Organization charts show the Group CISO, Group Chief Risk Officer and Group Chief Privacy Officer, the three division security and compliance leads, the Home Health HIPAA Privacy and Security Officers, the Consulting HIPAA compliance officer, the Staffing Vice President, Employment Compliance, and group internal audit reporting to the board audit committee. Treasury and operations confirm that no division accepts payment cards (clients pay by ACH or wire) and that no division offers or transports hazardous materials. No division is a social assistance organization

title: Group: HR roster by division
source_system: Group HR system (HR SaaS)
what_it_shows: 45,000 core employees: Staffing about 14,000, Consulting about 9,000, Home Health about 18,000, corporate about 4,000. Hire, transfer and termination events feed SYS-G1 identity governance

title: Group: FY2025 revenue by division
source_system: ERP general ledger; FY2025 Form 10-K segment note
what_it_shows: Revenue of about $18.0 billion: Staffing about $13.5 billion, Consulting about $2.7 billion, Home Health about $1.8 billion. Staffing revenue by line: Commercial about 58%, Professional about 21%, Healthcare Staffing about 15%, Managed Workforce Solutions about 6%

title: Group: payroll calendar and associate payroll volumes
source_system: GWP payroll engine reports (SYS-G4)
what_it_shows: About 230,000 temporary associates on assignment in an average week; about 860,000 different associates paid in 2025. Clients approve associate time by Monday 18:00, payroll runs Wednesday, and associates are paid Friday (about $190 million a week) by direct deposit or paycard through two ACH originating banks and a paycard program manager. Core employees are paid every two weeks

title: Group: intercompany agreement and BAA register
source_system: Group legal contract management system
what_it_shows: The intercompany BAA between corporate and Home Health (signed 2023-10) lists IT hosting, identity, SOC and EHR integration services; payroll is not among the listed services. The intercompany staffing agreement places about 1,100 Healthcare Staffing per diem clinicians a week with Home Health, working under Home Health's direct control. A 2024 statement of work covers Consulting's implementation of the Home Health EHR

title: Group: FY2025 Form 10-K cybersecurity disclosure and disclosure committee records
source_system: SEC filings; corporate secretary's records
what_it_shows: Form 10-K Item 1C describes board risk committee oversight, the Group CISO's reporting line and the use of group internal audit. The disclosure committee charter, chaired by the Group General Counsel, lists cybersecurity incidents among its matters. No exercise record of the disclosure playbook with a cross-division scenario and no method for estimating worker remediation cost were provided

title: Group: risk governance records
source_system: GRC tool; board and committee minutes
what_it_shows: Risk management strategy and risk standard approved by the board risk committee, with risk tolerance and acceptance authority by level; 2025 group and division risk registers; board risk committee minutes for 2025 to 2026 Q1 recording quarterly cyber reports; monthly division reports to the Group CISO; a metrics dashboard (MFA coverage, phishing, patching, fraud losses); group and Staffing strategy 2026; a stakeholder register; the group internal audit charter. The legal and regulatory register 2026 lists federal, state and contract duties; it has no entries for the Colorado SB26-189 or CPPA ADMT duties that start 2027-01-01

title: Group: policy and standards library
source_system: Group policy repository
what_it_shows: Group policies (2025) aligned to CSF 2.0; group standards for logging, identity, configuration, contingency, assessment and authorization, continuous monitoring, keys, supply chain risk and third parties; the group incident response plan (2025). Supplements for the three divisions are in the repository; the Home Health supplement is v2023, written at acquisition (2023-11), with no later alignment record

title: Group: common control catalog and inheritance matrices
source_system: GRC tool
what_it_shows: The common control catalog lists the controls corporate provides to the divisions and the GWP. Inheritance matrices on file: Staffing (2025) and Consulting (2026, including the Federal Solutions enclave). No Home Health inheritance matrix was provided (open request)

title: Group: SYS-G1 authentication, sign-in and conditional access policy export
source_system: Group identity platform admin console (SYS-G1)
what_it_shows: SSO with number-matching MFA for all workforce applications; phishing-resistant hardware keys for administrators; replay-resistant methods (number matching, FIDO2); lockout after 10 failed attempts with risk-based blocking; a system use notice at sign-in. Conditional access allows GWP applications from managed devices only (the associate self-service app excepted) and there is no network VPN path into the GWP accounts. The federation list includes every GWP staff application and the Federal Solutions enclave

title: Group: SYS-G1 identity governance export and service account register
source_system: Identity governance module (SYS-G1); workforce platform team service account register
what_it_shows: Joiner-mover-leaver workflows driven by HR events for all divisions; identifiers come from the HR record and are never reused; staff accounts inactive for 45 days are disabled; temporary and emergency accounts expire after 30 days; account events go to the SIEM; a high-risk account procedure lets HR and the SOC disable accounts (12 events in the period). Quarterly certification covers SOX and tier-1 applications; its scope does not include service accounts or E-Verify accounts. 41 GWP integration service accounts are listed in a separate register kept by engineers, outside identity governance

title: Group: privileged access management inventory, policy and logs
source_system: Privileged access management console (SYS-G1)
what_it_shows: Administrators hold separate privileged accounts; privileged roles are granted just in time with approval and session recording; privileged session logs go to the SIEM; vendor remote support uses PAM with named accounts, MFA and recording. The GWP role permission matrix keeps role administration, tokenization settings and logging with the platform security administrator role

title: Group: Q1 2026 access certification results and 2025 SOX IT general controls results
source_system: Identity governance module (SYS-G1); internal audit SOX workpapers
what_it_shows: Quarterly certification completed for SOX and tier-1 applications. The separation-of-duties rule set and the 2025 SOX IT general controls results record separate roles for payroll setup, payroll approval and bank file release

title: Group: endpoint configuration baseline
source_system: Endpoint management console (SYS-G3)
what_it_shows: Managed laptops lock after 10 minutes idle and use full-disk encryption and remote wipe; branch kiosks run in lockdown mode with application control

title: Group: SIEM data source inventory, logging configuration and detection rules
source_system: Group SIEM (SYS-G2)
what_it_shows: 24x7 SOC, in-house with managed security service provider overflow. Identity, endpoint, PAM, cloud audit and GWP application logs are onboarded, with an event list per GWP application and sample log records; Home Health EHR access logs, field tablet telemetry and the VMS tenant audit logs are not in the data source list, and Consulting repository sharing events are not reviewed. Rules include bulk export alerts in the payroll engine, off-hours access to I-9 document images, atypical staff use and hub egress volume; no rule covers bank-change velocity, repeat destination accounts or SaaS bulk exports. Correlation, threat intelligence enrichment and routing to division liaisons are configured

title: Group: SOC playbooks and incident case export, April 2025 to March 2026
source_system: Group case management system (SYS-G2)
what_it_shows: Incidents tracked in one case system with group playbooks (including payroll diversion and bulk export), the group severity scale, impact and magnitude estimates, forensic collection with chain of custody, and post-incident reports. Home Health cases are rated on Home Health's own 3-level scale. Case records show affected individuals by address of record, which for former associates can be old

title: Group: EDR coverage report
source_system: EDR console (SYS-G2)
what_it_shows: EDR on managed laptops, servers, cloud hosts and branch kiosks, with application control on kiosks. Of about 11,500 Home Health field tablets, 72% report the group EDR agent; the rest are managed by Home Health's legacy device management tool

title: Group: vulnerability scan, patch and advisory records, Q1 2026
source_system: Vulnerability scanner; patch management console; SOC advisory log
what_it_shows: Monthly authenticated scans of the payroll engine, integration platform and division hosts; patch service levels met for 96% of systems; payroll engine patches applied within 30 days (critical within 7). A vulnerability disclosure page and process are published. The SOC logs threat intelligence feeds and vendor advisories

title: Group: GWP penetration test report, 2026-03
source_system: Penetration testing firm report
what_it_shows: Annual test of the career sites, the associate self-service app and the payroll engine; findings are tracked in the GRC tool

title: Group: incident response plan (2025), draft notification matrix and exercise reports
source_system: Group SOC library; Group legal
what_it_shows: The group incident response plan (2025) names vendors, a liaison for each division and a communication plan for recovery progress and client and media statements; it does not include a GWP notification matrix, the E-Verify breach notice to DHS or a Home Health HIPAA path for visit-pay data. The draft notification matrix lists state breach, E-Verify, HIPAA, client contract and SEC clocks. Exercise reports for 2025 to 2026 Q1 cover quarterly technical playbook exercises; none covers the multi-regulator notification path, and GWP vendors and the VMS vendor did not take part

title: Group: cloud account inventory and landing zone design
source_system: Cloud consoles and asset inventory (SYS-G3); SD-WAN management
what_it_shows: One landing zone per provider with division and GWP accounts. Provider A hosts the corporate hub, the payroll engine and tokenization service, the integration platform, the workforce data hub, the I-9 archive and the Home Health visit-pay interface. Provider B hosts the GWP DR replica (warm standby), the backup vault and the Federal Solutions enclave. Cloud roles are federated from SYS-G1, with no local users except sealed break-glass accounts. SD-WAN connects about 650 sites with encrypted tunnels to the hubs; hubs have dual carriers

title: Group: guardrail policies, hub firewall and WAF configuration
source_system: Guardrail service; firewall management; API gateway console
what_it_shows: Guardrails enforce encryption, block public storage and restrict regions; a service allow list limits enabled services. The hub firewall inspects traffic and denies it by default between GWP and division accounts; workloads use private endpoints. The self-service API gateway has WAF rules with rate limits and bot rules on sign-in and bank-change APIs. Capacity reports track Friday pay peaks

title: Group: key management, encryption and tokenization settings
source_system: Key management service; payroll engine configuration
what_it_shows: Customer-managed keys for every data store; tokenization keys in a separate key ring with dual control; SSNs and bank account numbers tokenized inside the payroll engine and shown masked in the user interface; storage encrypted at rest; provider key services use FIPS-validated modules

title: Group: backup vault configuration and backup reports, January to March 2026
source_system: Backup service (provider B)
what_it_shows: Daily immutable backups of the payroll engine database, integration platform, data hub and I-9 archive, held in a separate provider B account with a separate backup identity; payroll engine database replication to provider B with a 15-minute RPO; weekly export of electronic Forms I-9 from the onboarding vendor; Federal Solutions enclave snapshots every 4 hours with daily immutable backups

title: Group: central log archive configuration
source_system: Central log archive account (SYS-G3)
what_it_shows: Write-once retention; logs kept 1 year searchable and 6 years archived; workload administrators cannot delete logs

title: Group: external TLS scan and file transfer configuration
source_system: Group TLS scanner; file transfer service
what_it_shows: The scan of public and interface endpoints found TLS 1.2 or higher only. The file transfer configuration sends bank files over SFTP with file encryption

title: Group Workforce Platform: component inventory and interface register
source_system: GWP component inventory; integration platform interface register
what_it_shows: Components: ATS and career sites with the AI ranking add-on and the recruiting assistant, the onboarding and electronic Form I-9 service and the credentialing service (vendor SaaS); the payroll and pay delivery engine with the self-service app and tokenization service; the integration platform; the workforce data hub; the I-9 archive; the DR replica. Interfaces: approved time from SYS-D1 (hourly), consultant timesheets from SYS-D2 (weekly), Home Health visit records from SYS-D3 (daily), two background screening providers, two ACH originating banks, the paycard program manager and the tax filing service. Interfaces validate time, rate and bank data; I-9 data is not sent to the data hub or the AI vendor

title: Group Workforce Platform: user and role report
source_system: GWP applications; SYS-G1 entitlement report
what_it_shows: About 9,600 staff users: recruiters about 6,100, onboarding and compliance about 1,400, payroll about 640, credentialing about 380, HR and associate service about 900, administrators about 180. About 1.1 million self-service accounts. Roles limit I-9 document images and consumer reports to onboarding and compliance staff and clinician medical files to credentialing staff. The 4 payroll roles (about 640 users) include the visit-pay record screen, which shows the fields received from Home Health. Recruiters and payroll users can export large result sets, including their own pipelines

title: Group Workforce Platform: data inventory and data map
source_system: GWP data map; database and storage reports
what_it_shows: About 7.2 million candidate profiles; about 3.4 million current and former worker records with SSNs and bank accounts (since 2014); about 1.9 million electronic Forms I-9 (since 2017) and about 0.9 million scanned paper forms (2009-2016); credential files for about 96,000 clinicians. The data map records where SSNs, bank accounts, I-9 images, consumer reports and credential files are stored. It does not list the visit-pay records

title: Group Workforce Platform: Home Health visit-pay interface specification
source_system: Integration platform interface register
what_it_shows: Live since 2024-04. Each visit record sent daily from Home Health scheduling for per-visit pay carries the patient's name, address, visit date and visit type; records cover about 214,000 patients so far. Records load to the payroll engine and nightly to the workforce data hub. No privacy review is attached to the specification

title: Group Workforce Platform: processing register and privacy impact assessment register
source_system: Group privacy office records
what_it_shows: Each GWP data category has a recorded authority and purpose (employment law, tax law, Form I-9, FCRA authorization, client contract); there is no entry for patient data in visit-pay records. The PIA register has no assessment of the visit-pay interface (2024) or the AI ranking add-on (2025). Notices at collection are posted on the career sites and in onboarding, including notices for California applicants and workers

title: Group Workforce Platform: self-service, candidate and client portal authentication settings
source_system: Payroll engine self-service configuration (SYS-G4); career site and ATS client portal settings
what_it_shows: Associates and employees sign in to self-service with an SMS one-time code, and the same code approves a bank-account change; an email notice follows each change; self-service locks after 5 failed attempts and sessions end after 10 minutes idle. Staff sessions in GWP applications end after 30 minutes idle and 12 hours absolute. Candidates use email-verified career-site accounts; ATS client portal users sign in with the portal's MFA

title: Group Workforce Platform: 2025 payroll fraud report and fraud case log
source_system: Group payroll fraud case log
what_it_shows: 690 fraudulent direct deposit changes in 2025 diverted about $1.9 million of pay, which the group repaid. The changes were made through associate self-service after an SMS one-time code. Bank changes are reviewed after a fraud complaint; fraud case reviews feed control changes

title: Group Workforce Platform: I-9 archive bucket settings
source_system: Object storage console (provider A)
what_it_shows: About 0.9 million scanned paper Forms I-9 (2009-2016) in object storage with encryption at rest and a restricted bucket policy. Object-level access logging is off, and the bucket keeps no per-object change history

title: Group Workforce Platform: DR test report (2026-02), payroll contingency plan and recovery runbook
source_system: GWP continuity library
what_it_shows: The 2026-02 failover of the payroll engine to the provider B replica met the 12-hour RTO; the test assumed the identity platform was available and did not restore from the immutable vault. The contingency plan covers repeating the prior payroll, paper Form I-9 onboarding and primary-source credential checks; no exercise record of the repeat-payroll procedure was provided. The recovery runbook restores the payroll engine from replica or backup, verifies backups before restore and replays approved time, with closure criteria

title: Group Workforce Platform: change, pipeline and secret records
source_system: Change management system; integration platform pipeline; secret store inventory
what_it_shows: Changes to payroll rules, interfaces, ATS workflows and AI add-on settings go through the change advisory board, with SOX approval for payroll and a security and privacy impact template. The pipeline runs code review, static analysis and dependency scanning and signs container images; bank files are hashed at creation and checked before release. Payroll engine and integration baselines are kept as infrastructure code, and SaaS tenant settings are exported monthly. The secret inventory lists static secrets for the 41 integration service accounts, 9 of them created more than 1 year before the export

title: Group Workforce Platform: AI ranking add-on vendor file and ATS configuration
source_system: ATS marketplace records; vendor management system; ATS configuration
what_it_shows: The AI ranking add-on was enabled through the ATS marketplace in 2025-05 and scores applicants for all three divisions. Its terms allow the vendor to train its model on candidate data. The vendor file holds no SOC 2 report, bias test results or due diligence record. Auto-advance of scores 75 and above has been on for Commercial requisitions since 2025-09; no change ticket for it was found. Branches have added knockout questions to the recruiting assistant outside the central question library, and candidates who fail a knockout question are closed automatically

title: Group Workforce Platform: NYC Local Law 144 bias audit, 2026-04
source_system: Independent bias auditor's report; NYC career pages
what_it_shows: The annual bias audit of the AI ranking tool covers NYC requisitions only; its summary is posted on the NYC career pages. The request for adverse impact results for other requisitions returned none

title: Group: vendor master, tiering and third-party risk records
source_system: Accounts payable vendor master; third-party risk tool; contract templates
what_it_shows: Vendors are tiered by data and criticality, and the vendor inventory lists supplier services. Contract templates carry security, breach notice and audit terms and confidentiality terms for contractors. Tier 1 onboarding due diligence records, annual reviews of tier 1 vendors and an offboarding checklist that returns or destroys data are on file. Client VMS integration terms do not address credentials. Tier 1 GWP vendors include the ATS, onboarding and credentialing vendors, the two screening providers, the two ACH banks, the paycard program manager and the tax filing service

title: Group: vendor SOC 2 reports and review records
source_system: Vendor portals; third-party risk tool
what_it_shows: SOC 2 Type 2 reports on file, reviewed annually, for both cloud providers, the identity, SIEM and EDR vendors, the ATS, onboarding and I-9 and credentialing vendors, the VMS vendor (recovery commitments RTO 8 hours, RPO 1 hour), the Consulting document repository vendor and the Home Health EHR vendor. The onboarding vendor's report and documentation describe a per-record change history for electronic Forms I-9. None is on file for the AI ranking add-on vendor. Vendor activity in group tenants is reviewed through these reports only

title: Group: training, phishing and acknowledgment records, 2025 to 2026 Q1
source_system: Learning management system
what_it_shows: Annual security awareness training and quarterly phishing exercises for all staff, including payroll diversion and bank-change scenarios for payroll and associate service staff; insider threat content for payroll, onboarding and credentialing roles; role training for onboarding (Form I-9, E-Verify tutorial), payroll and credentialing staff; annual I-9 training for onboarding staff; incident response training for SOC staff and division liaisons; acceptable use acknowledgments at hire and each year; Home Health monthly security reminders; Consulting quarterly HIPAA reminders and annual training

title: Group: personnel screening, confidentiality terms, job descriptions and sanctions log
source_system: Group HR system; HR case records
what_it_shows: Background checks under FCRA procedures before access to the GWP; confidentiality terms for staff, contractors and vendor staff; HR procedures; job descriptions and hiring standards; a sanctions procedure and sanctions log

title: Group: facilities and media disposal records
source_system: Badge system; facilities records; asset team certificates
what_it_shows: Badge access at branches, onboarding centers and offices; branch alarms, cameras and surge protection; laptop and storage media sanitization certificates from the group asset team; branch shred bin certificates from the shredding vendor

title: Group: retention schedule and deletion jobs
source_system: Records management system; deletion job list
what_it_shows: The retention schedule (approved 2025) sets periods for each record type, including Forms I-9 under the 8 CFR 274a.2(b)(2) formula, payroll and tax records. The deletion job list has no automated deletion for candidate profiles, consumer reports or visit-pay records; data goes back to 2014. The onboarding service keeps every Form I-9, and purge after the retention date is not automated. Recruiting contact center recordings are deleted after 2 years

title: Group: hiring and screening volumes, 2025
source_system: ATS and onboarding reports (SYS-G4)
what_it_shows: About 3.1 million applications; about 640,000 hires (about 610,000 of them Staffing associates), about 2,500 per business day; about 430,000 employment background checks through two screening providers. Requisitions are open in New York City, Illinois, Colorado and California

title: Group: AI tool discovery

what_it_shows: AI in use: AI-001 ranking add-on (since 2025-05, all divisions); AI-002 recruiting assistant with knockout questions; AI-003 clinician shift matching and pay-rate recommendation (in-house, on the data hub); AI-005 Home Health hospitalization risk model (EHR vendor, since 2025); AI-006 ambient documentation pilot in 6 Home Health agencies; AI-007 consultant drafting assistant; AI-008 claim denial-prediction model for 9 hospital clients; AI-009 enterprise generative AI pilot (3,000 users); AI-010 job ad drafting in the ATS

title: Staffing: Form I-9 program records

what_it_shows: I-9 procedure manual (2026) for every division; Section 2 tasks with deadline alerts in onboarding; the alternative remote examination procedure for remote Professional and Consulting hires; copies of documents kept with each electronic form; quarterly self-audit reports of 300 forms (2025 to 2026 Q1); vendor documentation of the electronic signature and of the onboarding service's system. No description of the scanned archive's indexing and retrieval was provided. An E-Verify outage procedure (Fla. Stat. 448.095 worked example) is on file

title: Staffing: FCRA and background screening records
source_system: Screening provider agreements; onboarding forms and settings
what_it_shows: Certifications on file with both screening providers; a standalone FCRA disclosure in use since 2024; authorizations e-signed in onboarding; adverse action letters sent by the provider when triggered by onboarding; consumer report PDFs kept in onboarding with no deletion setting; branch paper copies shredded with certificates

title: Staffing: site, client and clinician register
source_system: Front office CRM (SYS-D1); real estate records
what_it_shows: About 520 sites in 44 states and DC: 390 branches and 130 on-site offices at client facilities. About 14,000 active clients, including about 620 hospital and post-acute clients. About 28,000 Healthcare Staffing clinicians on assignment a week. The largest payroll and onboarding center is in Florida, with a second center in another state

title: Staffing: network segmentation report and asset inventory
source_system: SD-WAN management; asset management system
what_it_shows: Lobby kiosks are on a segmented network at 329 branches and on the staff network at 61 legacy branches. The asset system lists laptops, kiosks, network gear and badge and PIN time clocks by site, with hardware lifecycle dates

title: Staffing: hospital staffing agreements
source_system: Contract management system
what_it_shows: 214 hospital staffing agreements contain BAA or confidentiality terms; the shortest incident notice term is 48 hours. The agreements place clinicians under the hospital's direction and supervision. Some clients ask for associate SSNs for site badges

title: Staffing: Managed Workforce Solutions program records
source_system: VMS tenant (SYS-D1); program contracts; MWS operations manual
what_it_shows: Programs for 48 clients and about 1,900 suppliers run on one vendor VMS tenant that the division configures by hand with a checklist and operates (about 160 program staff); some program workers are payrolled through the GWP. Every MSP contract requires incident notice within 48 hours; 31 require a SOC 2 Type 2 report by 2027-12-31; service commitments sit in the 48 separate contracts, some of which define deletion at program end. On file: the service catalog, data flow diagrams, the operations manual and manual procedures, client billing and rate rules, invoice runs and delivery logs, invoice variance reports, Monday peak reports, change records and the change log, the tenant role matrix, VMS user reports, retention settings and the vendor recovery runbook. A job exports tenant audit logs; no review record of the exported logs was provided

title: Staffing: front office, time capture and client VMS integration configuration
source_system: Front office admin consoles (SYS-D1); integration allow lists
what_it_shows: Staff accounts are federated to SYS-G1 (federation list), with SSO and MFA for the VMS tenant; client portal users are managed by client administrators. About 400 client VMS integrations use shared service accounts and long-lived keys behind integration allow lists. Email data loss prevention runs in monitor mode. Time clocks come from a single timekeeping vendor and buffer punches locally for 72 hours

title: Staffing: contact center procedures and marketing compliance register
source_system: Contact center platform; call scripts; marketing compliance register
what_it_shows: Agents verify callers with knowledge-based checks before account changes, including bank changes, with supervisor review of repeat callers. Call recordings are kept 2 years and then deleted automatically. Associate requests arrive at branches and through a web request form. The marketing compliance register shows recruiting texts sent only to opted-in candidates

title: Consulting: engagement, client, contract and subcontractor register

what_it_shows: Health IT Advisory: about 4,200 consultants serving about 160 hospital and health-system clients. Workforce and HR Technology Consulting: about 3,100 consultants who configure clients' HR and payroll systems inside client tenants. Federal Solutions: about 1,700 staff on 11 federal civilian prime contracts and 4 subcontracts; no DoD contracts or subcontracts; no CUI designated. About 240 independent subcontractors. title: Consulting: client BAA register and subcontract template
source_system: Consulting compliance records
what_it_shows: Signed BAAs with all hospital and health-system clients; standard breach notice term 10 business days, with 23 clients at 72 hours; the register does not flag the 72-hour clients. title: Consulting: client-issued account and roll-off records

title: Consulting: Federal Solutions enclave configuration and records

EDR with automatic updates, weekly scans and real-time file scanning on all desktops and servers; monthly patching (2026 Q1 patch reports); snapshots every 4 hours and daily immutable backups. Badge access and a visitor log with escorts at the Federal Solutions office. Flow-down clauses in the 4 subcontracts; an annual FAR 52.204-21 self-assessment

title: Consulting: HIPAA business associate program records
source_system: Consulting compliance records
what_it_shows: An annual business associate risk analysis and self-assessment; the compliance officer's designation letter; a client notice procedure and a case procedure that maps repository files to client patients; documentation kept 6 years under the records schedule; engagement plans that limit data requests; engagement close checklists

title: Home Health: agency, census and payer report
source_system: Home Health EHR reporting (SYS-D3); CMS certification and payer enrollment records

title: Home Health: 2025 HIPAA risk analysis and evaluation
source_system: Home Health compliance records
what_it_shows: Annual risk analysis of the EHR, tablets and agency offices; it does not mention the visit-pay records sent to corporate. The 2025 evaluation plan does not list the controls Home Health inherits from the group

title: Home Health: field tablet device management console
